content: The causes of hyperlipoproteinemia can be categorized as familial (primary), acquired (secondary), or idiopathic. Familial hyperlipoproteinemia, also known as primary hyperlipoproteinemia, is primarily caused by genetic abnormalities. Examples of these genetic conditions include familial hypercholesterolemia, familial combined hyperlipidemia, and familial hypertriglyceridemia. Acquired hyperlipoproteinemia, also referred to as secondary hyperlipoproteinemia, often mimics the clinical presentation of primary forms. Common causes of secondary hyperlipoproteinemia include the use of certain medications such as diuretics, beta-blockers, and estrogens. Additionally, endocrine disorders like diabetes mellitus and hypothyroidism, metabolic disorders, and renal conditions such as renal failure can contribute to the development of secondary hyperlipoproteinemia. Life-threatening causes of hyperlipoproteinemia are those conditions that, if left untreated, may result in death or permanent disability within 24 hours.
